# Jose Ramon Martinez Saavedra — Full Profile

> VP of Innovation and Lead Scientist at Quside Technologies. Builds deployable quantum-randomness infrastructure for cybersecurity, high-performance computing, and post-quantum systems.

## Identity

- Name: Jose Ramon Martinez Saavedra
- Titles: VP of Innovation, Lead Scientist
- Organization: Quside Technologies S.L. (2018–present)
- Location: Barcelona, Spain
- Email: jrmsaavedra@gmail.com
- Website: https://joseramasa.github.io
- GitHub: https://github.com/joseramasa
- LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/in/jrmsaavedra

## Professional Focus

Takes quantum physics from the lab to real-world products. Designs and builds quantum random number generators, integrates them with post-quantum cryptography stacks, and pushes their use into high-performance computing and cybersecurity applications.

Leads Quside's R&D strategy, manages an international patent portfolio (30+ families; co-inventor in 8 across US, EP, CN, JP), and coordinates competitive public funding. Bridges the gap between photonics hardware and the software/systems that make it deployable at scale.

## Education

- MBA — Valar Institute (Quantic School of Business and Technology), 2024–2025
- PhD in Photonics (Cum Laude) — Universitat Politecnica de Catalunya / ICFO, 2014–2018. Advisor: F. Javier Garcia de Abajo
- MSc in Photonics — UPC, UAB, UB, ICFO, 2013–2014
- Licenciado en Fisica (Fundamental Physics) — Universidad Complutense de Madrid, 2008–2013
- Grado en Derecho (in progress) — Universitat Oberta de Catalunya, 2018–present

## Research Output

### Publications (22 total)

Journals: Nature, ACS Photonics, Physical Review B, Nano Letters, PNAS, npj Quantum Information, APL Quantum, Physical Review Applied, Journal of Electronic Packaging, Journal of Physics A.

Key publications:
- Lindbladian Learning with Neural Differential Equations (arXiv, 2026)
- Integration of QRNG with PQC algorithms (arXiv, 2025)
- Comparing pseudo- and quantum-random number generators with Monte Carlo simulations (APL Quantum, 2024)
- Loophole-free Bell inequality violation with superconducting circuits (Nature, 2023)
- Quantum computing with graphene plasmons (npj Quantum Information, 2019)
- Visible Optical Resonances in Electrically Doped DNA (ACS Photonics, 2019)
- Hot-electron dynamics and thermalization in small metallic nanoparticles (ACS Photonics, 2016)

## Projects

### NanophotonicsLab
Open browser-based nanophotonics simulation toolkit. Mie scattering, plasmonics, RCWA, BPM, laser calculators, and more. No installation required. https://nanophotonicslab.com

### El Fotonario
Interactive photonics education platform in Spanish. 9 courses, 145 exercises, 78 visualizations, 458-term glossary. Covers electromagnetic fundamentals through nanophotonics. https://joseramasa.github.io/fotonica/

### PQC Course
Open course materials for Post-Quantum Cryptography. Lecture notes (159 pages) and Beamer slides (69 frames) in LaTeX. https://github.com/joseramasa/pqc-course

### Con la Venia
Interactive visual novel for learning Spanish civil procedural law. Built with Ren'Py, deployed as web application. https://joseramasa.github.io/con-la-venia/

### Science Outreach Books
Author of chapters in three collaborative popular science books in Spanish (all CC-licensed):
- Ciencia, y ademas lo entiendo (Ch. 62 & 63)
- Ciencia, y yo quiero ser cientifico (Ch. 70)
- Ciencia y otras easy pieces (Ch. 37)
